title: A fresh EC2 instance bootstrapped from the runbook reaches an all-healthy stack with no undocumented manual step
statement: **Given** a clean EC2 instance and the documented bootstrap **When** the operator runs the provisioning path end to end **Then** every container reports healthy with no step missing from the runbook, on either subdomain.

title: The existing Playwright suite passes against the UAT URL — real PKCE round-trip + core governance loop
statement: AMENDED per OQ-066 — the original text named a method that is provably impossible. It said to run the suite with `E2E_KEYCLOAK_URL=https://uat.acmp.anas7ammo.dev/kc`, but global-setup seeds its fixtures through the Keycloak ADMIN REST API after taking a master-realm token, and the public 443 listener returns 404 for BOTH `/kc/admin` and `/kc/realms/master` BY DESIGN (measured, DEF-027; AC-081 rests on that deny). Only the METHOD is corrected below — the substance graded is unchanged. **Given** the UAT environment is live **When** the existing Playwright suite runs with `E2E_WEB_URL=https://uat.acmp.anas7ammo.dev`, so the browser drives the PUBLIC host and exercises the real deployed listener, and with `E2E_KEYCLOAK_URL` pointed at the box's Keycloak through an operator-side SSM port-forward — a deploy-time procedure requiring NO code change, NO fixed-password bypass in seed-users.sh, and NO relaxation of the `/kc/` deny — **Then** auth (real Keycloak PKCE round-trip), the core governance loop, and RTL/a11y specs pass. **And** the fixed-password `e2e-*` accounts the run seeds are DISABLED in the realm afterwards (`enabled: false`), never DELETED — disabling removes the login risk, which is real because their password is committed in `e2e/users.ts` and UAT's 443 is open to the internet, while preserving the Keycloak `sub`. Deleting them instead orphans their CommitteeMember rows permanently and duplicates them on the next run, because app-side identity is the `sub` and audit immutability means a member row can be deactivated but never removed (DEF-029, learned the hard way 2026-08-09).
source_span: Amended 2026-08-09 by OQ-066 (resolved, PE-186); cleanup clause corrected delete->disable per DEF-029 the same day.

title: Keycloak persists to SQL Server; no Postgres container exists; restart preserves realm + users
statement: **Given** the cloud stack **When** the operator inspects running containers and restarts Keycloak **Then** no postgres/keycloak-db container exists, Keycloak's data lives in the SQL Server 'keycloak' database, and the realm + users survive the restart (verifies ADR-0036).

title: Recording upload → S3 → presigned playback → delete works against a real bucket; no MinIO container exists
statement: **Given** the cloud stack with S3 configured **When** a Secretary/Chairman uploads a recording, a member plays it back, and it is deleted **Then** the object round-trips through the environment's S3 bucket, playback works in a browser (CSP media-src matches the presign host), and no minio container exists (verifies ADR-0035, FR-056).

title: seed-users.sh is idempotent, sets UPDATE_PASSWORD, and each seeded user logs in and JIT-provisions with the correct role
statement: **Given** a users.csv roster **When** seed-users.sh runs twice **Then** the second run is a clean no-op, seeded users carry a temporary password + UPDATE_PASSWORD required action, and after a real login each is JIT-provisioned as an ACMP member with the correct role (CON-007/CON-009 honored).

title: Backup → restore drill passes the 3→0→3 check for BOTH Acmp and keycloak, on Express
statement: **Given** the cloud stack on SQL Server Express **When** the operator runs the backup then restore drill **Then** both the Acmp and keycloak databases round-trip a 3→0→3 row-count check, with no reliance on backup compression (Express-incompatible) and no Postgres leg (verifies NFR-058, ADR-0033 as amended).

title: TLS valid, HSTS present, certbot renew --dry-run passes
statement: **Given** a provisioned environment **When** the operator inspects the endpoint and runs certbot renew --dry-run **Then** the Let's Encrypt certificate is valid for the subdomain, the HSTS header is present, and the dry-run renewal succeeds (DNS-01 via Route 53).

title: UAT stop → start returns healthy at the same DNS name within 10 minutes
statement: **Given** on-demand UAT is stopped **When** the operator starts the instance **Then** the Route 53 A record is updated to the new public IP by the boot-updater and the stack returns all-healthy at uat.acmp.anas7ammo.dev within 10 minutes (verifies NFR-057 restore posture).

title: Cross-environment isolation: the UAT IAM key is denied on the prod bucket; UAT Webex posts never reach the prod space
statement: **Given** per-environment IAM users, buckets, roles and Webex config **When** the UAT IAM key is used against the prod bucket, and UAT Webex is exercised **Then** the S3 call returns AccessDenied and no UAT notification reaches the production Webex space; the UAT box cannot alter the prod DNS record.

title: Budget alerts fire; the IAM deny brake is provisioned and proven by policy simulation; the EC2 stop action is provisioned against live instance IDs by the launch script
statement: AMENDED per OQ-064 — the original text ('the 120% auto-stop action is provisioned and dry-run verified') was unsatisfiable on three counts: it said 120% while 00-account.sh targets 100%; it described a tag-scoped EC2 stop that the AWS API cannot express (SsmActionDefinition takes explicit InstanceIds, no tag filter); and budget actions have NO dry-run facility at all — `execute-budget-action` genuinely fires the action, so 'dry-run verified' could only ever be satisfied by really tripping the brake. **Given** the acmp-monthly $60 budget **Then** (1) its SNS subscription is confirmed and a threshold notification has been observed to arrive; (2) `describe-budget-actions-for-budget` shows the IAM deny action at 100% ACTUAL, ApprovalModel AUTOMATIC, Status STANDBY, targeting the acmp-admin user with the acmp-budget-deny-new-spend policy; (3) `aws iam simulate-principal-policy` — which IS a real dry run, unlike anything in the budgets API — shows that policy returning implicitDeny/explicitDeny for the spend-creating actions it claims to block, evaluated against acmp-admin; (4) once P25 launches instances, the SSM STOP_EC2_INSTANCES action exists at 100% ACTUAL pinned to the LIVE instance IDs, created-or-updated by the launch script itself so a replaced instance re-points automatically rather than via a runbook step; and (5) it is recorded that the IAM deny constrains only the acmp-admin IAM user — the account root user cannot be restricted by IAM policy — so the brake is only real while CLI work is done as acmp-admin rather than root.

title: CI publishes all five images to ECR by OIDC with no long-lived key, and the two web images are genuinely per-environment

title: An in-app invite creates the Keycloak account and reveals its temporary password exactly once
statement: **Given** an Administrator or Secretary on Administration → Members **When** they invite a user with an email address and a full name **Then** the account exists in Keycloak flagged must-change-password-at-first-login, the response reveals a temporary password EXACTLY ONCE, and that password appears in NO log, NO persisted record and NO file — proven by asserting a second read of the invite does not return it.
source_span: DEC-038; ADR-0038. The 'shown once' clause is load-bearing: 'no email in v1' is a hard constraint, so a credential is put in front of a human, and the make-roster-passwords.sh CSV of 26 temporary passwords is the hazard this must not repeat.

title: Every role-assignment guard REFUSES, proven by forcing each refusal
statement: **Given** in-app role assignment **When** an actor (a) attempts to change their OWN roles, or (b) attempts a change that would leave the committee with ZERO Administrators **Then** the API REFUSES both, server-side, regardless of what the UI offers; **and When** Administrator or Chairman is granted **Then** it requires a separate explicit confirmation rather than being one option among others. Each clause is evidenced by a test that FORCES the refusal and asserts it happened — asserting only that the happy path works would reproduce the un-failable check this project has been bitten by repeatedly.
source_span: DEC-038 guards 1-3; ADR-0038. These four guards REPLACE the structural guarantee the design gave away: an app that cannot write roles cannot escalate privilege. DEC-038 records the operator accepting the residual risk that a Secretary can both invite an account and grant it Administrator.

title: A role change takes effect immediately, not at token expiry
statement: **Given** a signed-in user with an active session **When** their roles are changed in the app **Then** their Keycloak sessions are terminated, so the next request carries the new roles rather than the old ones lingering until the 60-minute idle timeout — proven by asserting the user's subsequent request no longer exercises the removed role, not merely that a logout call was issued.
source_span: DEC-038 decision 5; ADR-0038. Roles reach the app through the token and are cached on CommitteeMember at login, so without forced sign-out a REMOVED role would remain usable for up to an hour — the half of revocation that actually matters.

title: The roster lists invited people who have never signed in, from ACMP's own data
statement: **Given** a user invited through the app who has never signed in **When** an Administrator opens the member roster **Then** that person is listed and visibly marked `invited`, sourced from the invite record rather than from any Keycloak read at request time; **and When** they sign in for the first time **Then** JIT provisioning (ADR-0004) creates their CommitteeMember row, the invite is matched by Keycloak `sub` and marked consumed, and the person appears exactly ONCE — not twice.
source_span: DEC-038 (supersedes DEC-033); closes DEF-038. The 'exactly once' clause guards the seam between the invite record and JIT provisioning; DEF-029 makes a wrongly-created member row permanent, so duplication here cannot be cleaned up afterwards.

title: Guest access expires and the server refuses it, rather than the banner merely saying so
statement: **Given** a guest presenter invited for a meeting **When** the meeting's access window has passed **Then** the API REFUSES their requests and the page states that access has ended — proven by advancing past the expiry and asserting the refusal, not by reading the countdown; **and** the Keycloak account is disabled at expiry so the login itself stops working. The banner and the server MUST read the same value.
source_span: DEC-037; ADR-0038. The design promises 'Presenter access — read-only, and expires after the meeting' while NO expiry mechanism existed in code (only Delegation auto-expires). The page shows unpublished topic material to an EXTERNAL person, so a promise the server does not keep is an exposure, not a cosmetic gap.

title: Every identity change is attributed in the immutable audit chain
statement: **Given** any invite, role assignment, forced sign-out or guest-expiry action **When** it succeeds **Then** a hash-chained AuditEvent (INV-005) records who acted, on whom, what changed from and to, and when — proven by asserting the ROW EXISTS after a real change, never by asserting that a handler was called.
source_span: DEC-038 guard 4; ADR-0038. This is the ACTUAL control for the accepted SoD residual risk and it is DETECTION, not prevention — so it has to be real. Four fixed defects in this project (DEF-030/031/032, OQ-068) were controls that detected but never told, with the telling half asserted in a comment instead of tested.

title: A dirty form registers a beforeunload handler that calls preventDefault, and a clean form removes it
statement: **Given** a user is editing a form with unsaved changes **When** the form is dirty **Then** the page has registered a `beforeunload` handler that calls `preventDefault()` on a cancelable event — the only action a page can take to request the browser's unsaved-changes dialog — **and When** the form becomes clean **Then** that handler is removed. ⚠ NARROWED FROM AC-048 BY SC-014 UNDER DEC-051 d1, AND THE NARROWING IS THE POINT: the original asserted that the browser's built-in dialog is TRIGGERED, which no automation available here can prove — Playwright auto-dismisses native beforeunload dialogs and Chrome suppresses them without a prior user gesture (AV-157, operator decision PE-286). This asserts the application's ENTIRE possible contribution instead, which is testable and is tested.

title: A Decided topic can be closed, and closing is refused from every other status
statement:
**Given** topic TOP-2026-011 has reached `Decided`
**When** the Secretary closes it
**Then** its status becomes `Closed`, a `TopicClosedEvent` is raised, and the transition is written to the topic's immutable history with the acting user attributed.
**And Given** a topic in any status other than `Decided`
**When** a close is attempted
**Then** it is refused and the status is unchanged — the refusal is asserted, not assumed, because a transition guard that is never exercised is indistinguishable from an absent one.

title: A deferred topic returns to triage, and its recorded revisit date becomes actionable rather than decorative
statement:
**Given** topic TOP-2026-012 was deferred with reason "awaiting vendor confirmation" and a revisit date of 2026-09-01
**When** the Secretary returns it to triage
**Then** its status becomes `Triage`, a `TopicTriagedEvent` is raised, the original deferral reason remains in the immutable history (FR-044), and the topic reappears in the triage queue.
**And Given** a topic that is not `Deferred`
**When** a return-to-triage is attempted
**Then** it is refused and the status is unchanged.
**And** the revisit date shown on the topic detail is reachable by an affordance in the UI — the gap this criterion exists to close is that `RevisitOn` was already displayed with no way to act on it.

title: A disabled member can be reactivated and can actually sign in again — including a guest the expiry sweep disabled
statement:
**Given** Administrator Alice has deactivated member Bob, or the hourly guest-expiry sweep has disabled guest presenter Carol
**When** the Administrator reactivates that account
**Then** the member's status returns to `Active`, the action is audited with the acting Administrator attributed, and the member's historical votes, authorship and assignments remain intact and attributed (FR-020's guarantee is not disturbed).
**And Given** the reactivated account is a guest whose `AccessExpiresAt` is in the past
**When** they attempt to sign in after reactivation
**Then** they are **admitted** — proving the access window was explicitly set or cleared, not left stale.
⚠ This second clause is the whole point: `PrincipalRevalidator` refuses an expired window **independently of status**, so a reactivation that flips only `Status` produces an Active-but-refused member, which reads as fixed and is not.

**Given** topic TOP-2026-013 is `Rejected`, and topic TOP-2026-014 is `Closed`
**When** the Secretary reopens either one with the justification "new regulatory guidance changes the assessment"
**Then** the status becomes `Reopened`, the justification is recorded in the immutable history, a `TopicReopenedEvent` is raised, and the topic re-enters the triage workflow.
**And Given** a reopen attempted with an empty or whitespace-only justification
**When** it is submitted
**Then** it is refused — the reason is mandatory, matching the rejection/deferral rule in FR-044.

title: A Secretary converts a Decided topic to a different type: the original is retired to Converted with the reason recorded, a new topic of the target type is created carrying the original's attachments, comments and classification, and a typed original->successor link is written
statement:
**Given** a topic in status Decided
**When** a Chairman or Secretary converts it to a different topic type, supplying a conversion reason
**Then** the original moves to Converted and its status history carries the reason; **and** a NEW topic of the target type exists in Submitted, carrying the original's title, description, justification, streams, systems, tags, urgency, source and scope, plus its attachments (pointing at the SAME stored objects) and its comments (retaining their ORIGINAL author and timestamp); **and** a typed ConvertedTo relationship is recorded from the original to the successor; **and** an AuditEvent row is emitted against the original. **And** the conversion is refused from any status other than Decided, refused without a reason, and refused when the target type equals the current type - in each case leaving the topic un-retired.

title: A Restricted topic is readable only by Chairman/Secretary/Auditor, its owner and explicit grantees; excluded from every list surface and from search for everyone else, refused as NOT FOUND by key, and data already copied out of it is redacted at projection
statement:
**Given** a topic marked Restricted by a Chairman or Secretary
**When** any other principal reads the system
**Then** the topic is absent from the backlog, kanban, agenda pool, dashboards and reports **and absent from their totals**; absent from search results; and a direct read by key is refused as **404, not 403**, because a 403 confirms the topic exists. **And** the Chairman, Secretary, Auditor, the topic's Owner and any holder of an explicit per-topic capability grant (Owner/Assignee/Presenter) all still see it. **And** only the Chairman and Secretary may set or clear the classification - not the Owner - and it remains possible on a Decided, Closed or Converted topic. **And** data already copied out of the topic - agenda item title snapshots, published agendas and minutes, traceability relationship title snapshots, and notification bodies - is redacted at PROJECTION time and never by mutating the stored snapshot. **And** confidentiality only ever narrows: an unrestricted topic behaves exactly as before.

It is stated in the AC rather than split into a separate row so the criterion matches FR-163 as written and cannot be read as Met while an agenda still leaks a restricted title."}

title: Every routable endpoint requires authorization except health checks and the three Webex routes that cannot carry a bearer, each of which is authenticated another way
statement:
**Given** the API host with its real routing table
**When** every `RouteEndpoint` is enumerated from `EndpointDataSource`
**Then** every endpoint carries `IAuthorizeData` metadata **except** `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/api/webex/webhook`, `/api/webex/oauth/start` and `/api/webex/oauth/callback`. **And** those five are anonymous BY DESIGN and not unauthenticated: the two health routes are named by NFR-020 itself, and the three Webex routes are browser or server-to-server flows that cannot present a Keycloak bearer - the webhook is authenticated by an HMAC signature filter running before the handler with a 5-minute replay guard, `/start` by an operator-only setup key compared with `FixedTimeEquals` and failing closed to 404, and `/callback` only completes a flow whose single-use `state` cookie was minted by a key-gated `/start` in the same browser. **And** the enumeration is proven to have a subject before any conclusion is drawn from an absence: it must see more than 50 endpoints, more than 40 of them under `/api`. **And** every allowlisted route must still exist, so the list cannot rot into an excuse for a genuinely open endpoint.
source_span: NFR-020; docs/domain/security-controls.md; ADR-0004; DW-029 batch 1
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 1, DEC-064 d5", "why_the_existing_tests_were_not_enough": "RealJwtAuthTests proves the auth pipeline challenges correctly, but by probing THREE routes: anonymous -> 401, bogus bearer -> 401, health stays open. NFR-020's target is a claim about the WHOLE SET, and three spot checks cannot establish it - a new endpoint group added without RequireAuthorization() would not be one of the three probed. The enumeration control was BUILT for this AC rather than the AC being written around what happened to already be tested.", "found_on_first_run": "Two endpoints with no authorization metadata - /api/webex/webhook and /api/webex/oauth/start. Reading them showed both have real compensating controls, so the finding was in MY allowlist, not in the product. The allowlist now names the mechanism for every entry."}

title: An enriched audit row records all eight fields FR-151 names, with the timestamp in UTC, and the stored hash recomputes
statement:
**Given** an enriched (v2) audit event
**When** the row is read back
**Then** it records all eight fields FR-151 names: entity type (`SubjectType`), entity ID (`SubjectId`), action type (`Action`), actor user ID (`ActorUserId`), timestamp (`OccurredAt`), before-state (`BeforeJson`), after-state (`AfterJson`) and correlation ID (`CorrelationId`). **And** the timestamp is UTC - a zero offset - because FR-151 says UTC and a local-time audit trail cannot be ordered against another machine's. **And** the row is internally consistent: the stored hash recomputes from its own canonical payload, so a field cannot be edited without detection. **And** the legacy v1 columns still mirror action and actor, so pre-enrichment readers keep working.
source_span: FR-151; ADR-0009; DW-029 batch 1
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 1, DEC-064 d5", "gap_closed": "FR-151 names EIGHT fields; AuditEventEnrichmentTests.Enriched_row_captures_the_full_field_set_and_is_v2 asserted SEVEN. The timestamp was the unasserted one - the field every 'who did what WHEN' question reads, and the one whose UTC-ness the requirement states explicitly. Writing the AC around the seven that were tested would have been exactly the hollow verdict this programme exists to stop, so the assertion was added."}

title: Selecting Arabic sets dir=rtl and lang=ar on the document element, and no component stylesheet uses a physical left/right property
statement:
**Given** a user selects Arabic
**When** the locale is applied
**Then** `dir="rtl"` and `lang="ar"` are set on the **document element** - ``, not a wrapper - because a portaled dialog escapes a wrapper and would read LTR inside an RTL page. **And** selecting English sets `dir="ltr"` and `lang="en"`, so the control reverses cleanly rather than latching. **And** no component stylesheet declares a physical-side property (`padding-left`, `margin-right`, `border-left`, and the rest); layout is expressed in logical properties throughout, which is what makes the mirroring automatic rather than hand-maintained per rule. **And** the target is literally zero such declarations, not merely few.
source_span: NFR-036; ADR-0012; DW-029 batch 1
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 1, DEC-064 d5", "both_halves_verified": "NFR-036 has two clauses and each has its own control: direction.test.ts covers the dir/lang half and rtl-physical-direction.test.ts covers the logical-properties half. The second is the one usually left as an aspiration - a physical-side count was taken independently and is genuinely 0 across styles/ and features/*/, so the target is met rather than approximately met.", "stale_reference_noted": "direction.test.ts's header comment cites AC-040, which is Superseded and belongs to FR-004. The comment is stale, not wrong-headed; NFR-036 genuinely had no active AC, which is why this row exists. Not edited here - it is a comment, and touching it would put an unrelated source change in a package batch."}

title: Superseding an ADR links both records in both directions, freezes the prior as Superseded, preserves both, and leaves neither editable
statement:
**Given** an Approved ADR
**When** it is superseded by a new ADR
**Then** the prior moves to `Superseded` and carries `SupersededByAdrId` pointing at its successor, and the detail read resolves the peer key in BOTH directions so the page can render 'Supersedes' and 'Superseded by'. **And** both records are PRESERVED - the prior is still retrievable by its own key after the event, never deleted. **And** both are IMMUTABLE: content edits go through `UpdateDraft`, which calls `RequireStatus(AdrStatus.Draft)`, so neither an Approved nor a Superseded ADR can be revised. **And** supersession is only possible FROM Approved, and both the successor's approval and the prior's supersession are audited as separate events.
source_span: FR-101; ADR-0006; DW-029 batch 2
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 2, DEC-064 d5", "no_new_code_needed": "Unusually for this programme, FR-101 was fully covered before the AC existed. AdrHandlerTests.Supersede_authors_a_new_approved_adr_and_freezes_the_prior_with_both_links covers the links, the freeze, the preservation and both audit events; AdrTests.UpdateDraft_replaces_content_and_options_only_while_draft FORCES the immutability refusal, and AdrTests.Supersede_freezes_the_prior_with_a_backlink_and_only_from_approved covers the from-Approved guard. The AC was written to the requirement and then the coverage was checked against it - not the reverse."}

title: Cancelling an action requires a bilingual reason and the cancelled action is preserved with that reason intact, never deleted
statement:
**Given** an open action
**When** a Secretary cancels it
**Then** the command is REFUSED unless it carries a reason in both EN and AR - the reason is mandatory, not optional metadata. **And** the action moves to `Cancelled` rather than being removed: it is still retrievable by its key afterwards, which is the whole point of the requirement, because an action that vanishes takes its history with it. **And** the cancellation reason is preserved on the record and readable in both languages, so the audit trail explains WHY and not merely THAT.
source_span: FR-086; DW-029 batch 2
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 2, DEC-064 d5", "gap_closed": "FR-086 names three clauses - mandatory reason, remains in history, never deleted - and ActionHandlerTests.Cancel_handler_moves_to_cancelled asserted only the status. Preservation was proven INCIDENTALLY: the read-back used a null-forgiving dereference, so a delete would have surfaced as a NullReferenceException rather than as a named failure. That is a real signal but an accidental one, and the reason's survival was not asserted at all. Both are now explicit. The mandatory-reason clause was already covered by Cancel_validator_requires_a_bilingual_reason."}

title: The API is bearer-only with no cookie authentication scheme, so no ambient credential exists for a cross-site request to ride
statement:
**Given** the production authentication wiring
**When** the registered authentication schemes are enumerated
**Then** NO scheme uses a cookie handler - checked on the HANDLER TYPE, not the scheme name, so a cookie scheme registered under any custom name is still caught. **And** the default authenticate scheme IS JWT bearer, because 'no cookie scheme' on its own is equally true of an app with no authentication at all; the two together say bearer-and-only-bearer. **And** the enumeration is proven to inspect PRODUCTION wiring rather than the test harness: the test authentication scheme must be absent from the list. **THIS IS HOW NFR-022 IS SATISFIED, and the reasoning is the criterion:** the anti-forgery token and the SameSite policy that NFR-022 names both defend against an AMBIENT credential the browser attaches by itself. A bearer token must be attached deliberately by the caller on every request, so cross-site request forgery has nothing to forge with. The control therefore guards the PREMISE - adding a cookie scheme would silently reintroduce the attack and would make one of NFR-022's two named mechanisms genuinely required.
source_span: NFR-022; docs/domain/security-controls.md; DW-029 batch 2
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 2, DEC-064 d5", "target_clause_note": "NFR-022's literal target is '0 CSRF vulnerabilities per OWASP ZAP scan'. No ZAP scan runs in this repository's CI, so that clause is NOT claimed as verified by this AC and no verdict pretends otherwise. What IS verified is the structural property that makes the vulnerability class inapplicable. If a ZAP scan is ever added, it belongs against this AC as additional evidence.", "hollow_first_draft": "The first version of this control ran on AcmpWebApplicationFactory, which calls AddAuthentication(TestAuthHandler.SchemeName) and REPLACES the real schemes - so it inspected the harness and would have passed regardless of what production registers. It was caught only because the default-scheme case failed loudly with 'Test' instead of 'Bearer'. The suite now uses a factory that leaves authentication alone AND asserts the test scheme is absent, so the harness cannot leak back in unnoticed. Recorded because the near-miss is more instructive than the fix."}

title: Every ballot is attributed to its voter, the cast is audited, and the results surface shows both individual choices and aggregate totals
statement:
**Given** a vote with eligible voters
**When** a voter casts a ballot
**Then** the ballot is recorded AGAINST THAT VOTER - the read model exposes the ballot keyed by `VoterUserId` with the voter's display name and their choice - and the cast emits a `Decisions.BallotCast` audit event. **And** the results surface shows BOTH halves that NFR-029 names: the individual ballots and the aggregate option counts, with the frozen server tally authoritative once the vote is Closed and a derived live tally while it is Open. **And** there is no anonymization pathway: `Ballot.VoterUserId` is a non-nullable string set once at construction with a private setter, so the domain has no operation that can detach a ballot from its voter - anonymity is absent by construction, not by policy.
source_span: NFR-029; ADR-0010; DW-029 batch 4
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 4, DEC-064 d5", "evidence_split": "Three clauses are auto-tested; the fourth ('no anonymization pathway') is STRUCTURAL ANALYSIS, not a measurement, and the verdict says so rather than dressing it as a test. There is no test that asserts the absence of an anonymize operation, because an absence needs an instrument and no natural one exists here - what exists is a non-nullable field with a private setter and no mutator, which is a stronger guarantee than a test would be but is established by reading the type, not by running it.", "no_divergence_found": "Unlike NFR-025 in the previous batch, the visibility clause here does NOT diverge. NFR-029 says individual choices are 'accessible to Auditor and Chairman' AND that 'the results view displays both individual choices and aggregate totals' - the second clause makes wider visibility consistent with the requirement rather than a violation of it, since the whole point of ADR-0010 is that v1 voting is not anonymous."}

title: A meeting recording's playback URL is mintable only by Chairman, Secretary or Auditor, and every successful mint writes an audit row
statement:
**Given** a meeting with an uploaded recording
**When** a principal requests its playback URL
**Then** the request succeeds ONLY for the three roles NFR-025 names - Chairman, Secretary, Auditor - and every other role is refused with 403, including Member, Reviewer and Submitter, who can open the meeting itself perfectly well. **And** each successful mint writes a `Meetings.RecordingAccessed` audit row naming the meeting, so 'all access to transcript content shall generate an audit log entry' is satisfied rather than aspirational. **And** the row is written only AFTER a URL is actually minted: a meeting with no recording returns 404 and writes NOTHING, because it grants nothing - the row must mean 'a capability was handed out', not 'someone asked'. **And** the URL itself never appears in the audit row, because NFR-027 keeps presigned URLs out of logs and an audit row is a log. **And** the READ set is not the WRITE set: the Auditor may mint a playback URL but may not upload or delete a recording, which stays Chairman/Secretary.
source_span: NFR-025; docs/domain/security-threat-model.md; ADR-0009; DEF-094; DW-029 batch 6
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 6, closing DEF-094 under DEC-064's disposition", "why_minting_is_an_access_event": "A presigned URL is a BEARER-LESS CAPABILITY: whoever holds it can stream the recording for its whole TTL with no further authentication. So the mint - not some later download the application never sees - is the only moment access can be recorded at all. That is also why the role gate belongs on this read and not only on the upload.", "built_not_reworded": "The operator chose to build the requirement rather than narrow it to match the code. Two existing tests had encoded the divergence as intent - one literally read 'any member can fetch the presigned playback URL' - and were changed with the behaviour. An AC written before that decision would have had to record Not-met."}

title: The audit table is append-only at the DATABASE, not merely by application convention: the app's own SQL login is denied UPDATE and DELETE on it
statement:
**Given** a real SQL Server with the production grants applied
**When** the application's own SQL login attempts to UPDATE or DELETE an audit row
**Then** the DATABASE refuses it - the application role may INSERT and SELECT on the audit table and nothing else. **And** the refusal is not a property of the ORM or of careful application code: a least-privileged service login holding `db_datawriter`, which can write every other table, is still denied audit mutation. **And** the append and read paths continue to work under the same grants, so the control narrows without breaking the log it protects.
source_span: NFR-040; ADR-0009; docs/domain/audit-and-records.md; DW-029 batch 7
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 7, Must-priority sequencing (DEC-064 d5)", "stronger_than_written": "NFR-040 asks for 0 UPDATE/DELETE statements targeting the audit table IN APPLICATION CODE - a property of the source, which a future commit could quietly violate. What is actually built is stronger: the DATABASE denies the mutation to the application's own login, so even code that tried would fail at runtime. The AC is written to the stronger property because that is what the tests prove; a source-only criterion would have been satisfiable by a grep and would have said less."}

title: A state transition and its audit row commit together or not at all, and the hash chain does not fork under concurrency
statement:
**Given** a command that transitions a governed entity
**When** it commits
**Then** the entity change and its audit row land in THE SAME DATABASE TRANSACTION - proven in both directions, because one direction alone is not the requirement: a successful cast commits both the ballot and its audit row, AND an audit append that fails ROLLS THE BALLOT BACK. A state transition without an audit entry is impossible rather than merely discouraged. **And** a REFUSED command still audits: a double-cast denial's audit row survives the thrown command, so the record shows attempts as well as successes. **And** under concurrency the guarantee holds without corrupting the log: concurrent commands all commit without forking the audit hash chain, and concurrent DENIALS likewise record through the retry without forking it. **And** the enriched row carries populated before/after state rather than empty placeholders.
source_span: NFR-042; ADR-0009; docs/domain/audit-and-records.md; DW-029 batch 7
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 7, Must-priority sequencing (DEC-064 d5)", "why_both_directions_matter": "'Every state transition generates an audit entry within the same TX' is only half-tested by a commit-together case. The load-bearing test is Audit_append_failure_rolls_the_ballot_back: without it, an implementation that wrote the audit row on a best-effort basis outside the transaction would pass the happy path and still violate the requirement in exactly the situation the requirement exists for.", "chain_note": "The concurrency cases are included in the criterion rather than treated as separate hardening, because an audit chain that forks under load is not an audit chain - the same-transaction guarantee would hold per command while the log as a whole stopped being verifiable."}

title: No module references another module's types, and the layering holds, enforced as a compiled assembly-dependency test rather than by review
statement:
**Given** the compiled assemblies
**When** their references are inspected
**Then** NO module depends on another module: every one of the thirteen modules that exist - Membership, Topics, Meetings, Decisions, Actions, Risks, Dependencies, Governance, Research, Knowledge, Notifications, Traceability and Integrations/Webex - has its own boundary assertion. **And** the layering holds within a module: Domain depends on neither Application nor Infrastructure and does not reference EntityFrameworkCore, and Application does not depend on Infrastructure. **And** the enforcement is a TEST OVER COMPILED ASSEMBLIES, not a convention or a review checklist, so a violation fails the build rather than waiting to be noticed - which is what makes ADR-0001's in-process-contract rule survive contact with a hurry.
source_span: NFR-047; ADR-0001; ADR-0002; docs/domain/repository-structure.md; DW-029 batch 7
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 7, Must-priority sequencing (DEC-064 d5)", "precision_about_the_module_list": "⚠ NFR-047 names SIXTEEN canonical modules; only THIRTEEN exist as module projects, and the AC says thirteen deliberately rather than claiming the requirement's own list is covered. The three that are absent are absent by design, not by omission: DIAGRAMS does not exist because Tarseem is deferred indefinitely (DEC-028, DW-011); REPORTING is an SPA feature composed client-side over existing APIs, not a backend module; and AUDIT&RECORDS and PLATFORM live in the shared kernel (Acmp.Shared) which every module may reference by construction, so a boundary assertion against them would be meaningless. Verified by listing src/Modules - 13 directories - and matching each against a named test."}

title: No secret reaches source or images: a gating full-history gitleaks scan runs on every push with a triaged allowlist that no longer exempts whole file types
statement:
**Given** the repository and its complete commit history
**When** CI runs
**Then** gitleaks scans with `--exit-code=1`, so a finding BLOCKS rather than warns, and it scans the FULL history (`fetch-depth: 0`) rather than the diff - a secret committed and later deleted is still a leaked secret. **And** the allowlist is triaged entry by entry, with each exemption naming why it is not a secret; it does NOT exempt a whole file type. **And** application secrets are supplied at runtime through environment variables or a secrets manager, never literals in source, build artifacts or container images.
source_span: NFR-024; docs/domain/security-controls.md; DW-029 batch 8
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 8, Must-priority sequencing (DEC-064 d5)", "the_clause_that_earns_its_place": "'no longer exempts whole file types' is in the criterion because of DEF-081: the allowlist USED to carry a '.*\\.md' path entry, which exempted EVERY markdown file, and the gating full-history scan passed over 153 commits while real finding sites sat in .md files. A green scan with a hole that size is worse than no scan, so the AC asserts the shape of the allowlist and not merely that the job exists and is green. This is the same failure family as DEF-078's healthcheck that evaluated zero checks."}

title: Line coverage is gated in CI at a threshold well above the requirement's floor, enforced PER FILE as well as globally
statement:
**Given** the test run
**When** the coverage gate executes
**Then** the build FAILS unless line coverage meets the threshold, so coverage is a gate and not a report nobody reads. **And** the threshold is enforced PER FILE as well as globally - a global average can hide an untested file behind well-covered neighbours, which is exactly what a domain-logic floor is meant to prevent. **And** the enforced threshold EXCEEDS the requirement's floor: NFR-048 asks for at least 80% on domain logic and the gate is set at 95% across the board.
source_span: NFR-048; ADR-0016; docs/validation/test-strategy.md; DW-029 batch 8
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 8, Must-priority sequencing (DEC-064 d5)", "why_per_file_is_the_load_bearing_clause": "coverlet's own threshold is per-ASSEMBLY only, which is why scripts/check-coverage.mjs exists at all: a per-assembly or global number can sit comfortably above 95% while a single new domain file has none. The per-file rule is what makes the number mean what a reader assumes it means.", "stronger_than_written": "NFR-048 scopes its 80% to DOMAIN LOGIC specifically; the gate applies 95% to every measured file in the solution, so the requirement's floor is cleared with margin and by a wider rule than it asks for. The AC is written to what is enforced."}

title: Every dependency is version-bounded, and High/Critical advisories block the build in both ecosystems rather than merely raising a pull request
statement:
**Given** the .NET and npm dependency manifests
**When** they are inspected
**Then** NO dependency is declared with a wildcard or an unbounded range - every `.csproj` PackageReference carries an explicit version and every npm dependency a bounded specifier. **And** known High/Critical advisories BLOCK the build in both ecosystems, through `check-vulns.mjs` for .NET and `check-npm-audit.mjs` for npm, each with an explicit triage allowlist where every exemption records why it does not apply to ACMP. **And** Dependabot is configured across all four ecosystems - nuget, npm, docker and github-actions - so updates arrive continuously rather than on a manual sweep.
source_span: NFR-051; docs/domain/security-controls.md; DW-029 batch 8
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 8, Must-priority sequencing (DEC-064 d5)", "the_48_hour_clause": "⚠ NFR-051 says Dependabot 'shall be configured to alert on known CVEs within 48 hours'. A LATENCY TARGET CANNOT BE VERIFIED FROM THE REPOSITORY - it depends on GitHub's advisory feed, not on anything in this codebase - and this AC does not claim it. What it asserts instead is the stronger practical property: the gates run on EVERY push and pull request and FAIL the build, so a High/Critical advisory stops work at the next CI run rather than being announced within two days. The requirement's intent is met by a faster mechanism than the one it names; its literal words are not independently measurable here and are not claimed.", "triage_not_suppression": "Both gates were deliberately built with a triage allowlist rather than a blanket audit-level flag - the note in ci.yml records that `npm audit --audit-level=high` was replaced precisely because it had no triage mechanism, so a single unfixable advisory would otherwise have forced the whole gate to be disabled."}

title: A closed vote and an issued decision are frozen at their immutability event, and correction is only possible by supersession
statement:
**Given** a vote that has closed or a decision that has been issued
**When** any change to it is attempted
**Then** it is REFUSED by a domain guard - a closed vote is forward-only and immutable, and its tally is frozen with the counter recorded at close rather than recomputed later. **And** an issued decision cannot be re-superseded, so the supersession chain cannot be rewritten after the fact. **And** supersession is only available FROM an issued decision: attempting it against a draft trips the domain guard, so the correction path cannot be used to bypass the lifecycle. **And** correction is therefore possible ONLY by authoring a new superseding record with a back-link to the prior, never by mutating the frozen one.
source_span: NFR-041; ADR-0009; docs/domain/audit-and-records.md; DW-029 batch 9
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 9, Must-priority sequencing (DEC-064 d5)", "guards_proven_by_refusal": "Every clause here is covered by a test that FORCES the refusal rather than merely exercising the happy path - Vote_is_forward_only_and_immutable_after_close, Issued_decision_is_immutable_no_re_supersede, Supersede_on_a_draft_prior_trips_the_domain_guard. That matters for an immutability requirement more than for most: a happy-path test proves you CAN write the record, never that you cannot rewrite it."}

title: UI strings live in the react-i18next resource files with EN/AR parity, and a separate gate reads the components to prove none was typed into JSX instead
statement:
**Given** the SPA
**When** CI runs
**Then** BOTH of NFR-035's clauses are gated, by two different instruments, because one cannot see what the other checks. **Externalization:** `check-i18n.mjs` fails the build on any EN/AR key-parity gap and additionally on mojibake - Arabic written as Latin-1-decoded UTF-8, a defect class this project has actually hit. **No hardcoded display strings:** `check-hardcoded-strings.mjs` reads the COMPONENTS and fails on any JSX text node containing words, which the parity check is structurally incapable of noticing - a label typed straight into JSX never enters either resource file, so parity stays perfect while the string ships untranslatable. **And** the component gate is proven to have a subject: it refuses to report a clean tree over fewer than 50 components, so it cannot pass by scanning nothing.
source_span: NFR-035; ADR-0012; DW-042; DW-029 batch 10
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 10, closing DW-042 under DEC-064's build-the-missing-half policy", "two_instruments_one_requirement": "The criterion names both gates deliberately. NFR-035 reads as a single sentence but contains two independent claims, and the obvious instrument - the i18n gate - can only ever verify the first. Writing an AC that cited check-i18n alone would have recorded Met for a half-guarded requirement while looking thoroughly evidenced, which is the exact shape this programme keeps finding in OTHER requirements.", "scanner_scope": "⚠ The scanner reads JSX TEXT NODES. It does NOT yet flag display text passed as an ATTRIBUTE - aria-label, title, placeholder - which is also user-visible. That is a real remaining gap, deliberately not claimed by this AC, and it needs a different matcher because attributes cannot be distinguished from non-display attributes by position alone."}

title: User input is validated server-side before it reaches persistence, no user input reaches SQL as concatenated text, and a gating SAST job scans the whole tree for injection vectors
statement:
**Given** every write command in the modular monolith
**When** it carries user-supplied input
**Then** that input is validated server-side before it reaches persistence - by a FluentValidation validator bound to the command through the shared ValidationBehavior pipeline, or by a guard inside the domain aggregate the handler calls. **And** no user input reaches SQL as concatenated text: every query is EF Core LINQ, full-text search goes through EF.Functions, and the single DbCommand.CommandText in the whole of src/ is a compile-time constant that takes no parameters at all. **And** the scan that would DETECT an injection vector is a gating CI job over the whole tree, proven to fire on this codebase rather than assumed to.
source_span: NFR-021; docs/domain/security-controls.md; .github/workflows/security.yml; DW-029 batch 13
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 13", "three_clauses_one_requirement": "NFR-021 reads as one sentence and contains three independent claims - validate server-side, never concatenate SQL, and prove it with a scanner. The criterion names all three because each needs a different instrument: a command census for the first, a raw-SQL sweep for the second, and the CI SAST job for the third. An AC citing only the SAST job would have recorded Met for a requirement whose first clause was never examined.", "validation_is_non_uniform": "Two mechanisms satisfy clause one, not one. 78 of 116 command types carry an AbstractValidator; the rest are guarded in the domain or carry only identifiers. That is WHY the census had to be read command by command - a count of validators alone reads as a 38-command hole and would have produced a false defect."}

title: Each of the five canonical workflows has both a happy-path and a failure-path test through the real HTTP pipeline, above the criterion's floor of ten
statement:
**Given** the five canonical workflows named by the requirement - topic intake, agenda creation, meeting and minutes, vote and decision, action lifecycle
**When** the solution test suite runs in CI
**Then** each workflow has at least one end-to-end happy-path test AND at least one failure-path test, every one exercised through the real HTTP pipeline via WebApplicationFactory with authorization, model binding, the MediatR pipeline and the exception handler all in play. **And** the total is above the criterion's floor of ten, counted as named tests per workflow rather than as a project-wide test count, because a floor met by ten tests of one workflow would satisfy the number while failing the requirement.
source_span: NFR-049; ADR-0016; docs/validation/test-strategy.md; tests/Acmp.Api.Tests; DW-029 batch 13
custom_attributes: {"added_by": "DW-029 batch 13", "counted_per_workflow_not_in_total": "The requirement's own target arithmetic is 5 workflows x 2 = at least 10, so the honest instrument counts per workflow and not in total. Acmp.Api.Tests holds 49 files and would clear a bare count of ten many times over while leaving a workflow uncovered; the verdict therefore names the specific happy-path and failure-path test for each of the five.", "provider_divergence_not_claimed": "The test-strategy narrative describes these as running against a real SQL Server via Testcontainers. AcmpWebApplicationFactory substitutes EF InMemory for every module context. The criterion as written names no provider, so this AC is measured against the criterion and deliberately does not certify the narrative. The real-SQL-Server project is Acmp.Integration.Tests."}
